What it usually means & typical next ste: You referenced <GraphName>.<collection> but that collection isn’t declared in the graph metadata. Fix → add the collection to the graph definition or correct the graph-qualified name.
You pointed at a simple-table collection (raw DB table) that hasn’t been registered in the graph. Fix → create a SimpleTableCollection entry—or switch to the correct registered collection.
Example exception text (verbatim): Unrecognized term of simple table collection 'Customers' in graph 'Broker': 'Customers'

What it usually means & typical next ste: The collection name is clearly a template placeholder such as EXAMPLE_GRAPH or PLACEHOLDER_TABLE. Fix → replace the placeholder with the actual collection name before running the query/script.
The name matches an existing collection except for letter-case (identifiers are case-sensitive). Fix → use the exact case found in the metadata, or normalise identifiers.

A bare term that looks like a field/metric or a plural/singular variant rather than a real collection. Fix → qualify it as collection.property or check if you meant the singular/plural collection already registered.

A keyword/operator (e.g., WEEK, TODAY, NOW, ISOWEEK, DISTINCT) was written as if it were a column or constant instead of a function call. Fix → add parentheses and pass an argument (e.g., WEEK(date_col)), or remove the stray identifier if you meant a column name.
Example exception text (verbatim): PyDough nodes WEEK is not callable. Did you mean to use a function?

What it usually means & typical next ste: An aggregate such as NDISTINCT was invoked with a literal list or other non-expression argument that PyDough hasn’t implemented yet. Fix → wrap each argument in a PyDough expression (e.g., pass a column reference) or wait for list-style support in a future release.
Example exception text (verbatim): PyDough does not yet support non-expression arguments for aggregation function Function[NDISTINCT]

What it usually means & typical next ste: Any error that does not meet the requirements of any other error class. Only use this class as a last-resort.
